gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Ubiquiti sells the UniFi UNAS 2, a 2-bay NAS with 2.5GbE, for $199.00 on its own US store ($219.00 with surcharge included) with a PoE++ adapter in the box. That makes it the cheapest 2.5GbE 2-bay unit in this category, under the Asustor AS1202T at $199.99 and the TerraMaster F2-425 at $254.99.
standout_why: I compared against ComputingForGeeks (cited, 2026-10-24), nas.kuibu.net (cited) and Starry Hope (cited, 2026-10-31). ComputingForGeeks lists DS225+, DXP2800, F2-425, DXP2800 GT, DS223j and DH2300 with Amazon prices from 2026-10-24. Starry Hope lists maker-store prices for DXP2800 ($389.99), DH2300 ($239.99), F2-425 Plus and DS225+. Kuibu gives only rough prices (~$300 DS224+/DS225+, ~$370-380 DXP2800). None of the three mentions the UNAS 2 or any Ubiquiti NAS. None of them backs ChatGPT's $296.99 Walmart DXP2800 price either: both pages that price the DXP2800 put it at $389.99. I could not open the other results (B&H, Newegg, Micro Center, Walmart, UGREEN, TerraMaster all returned 403, 429 or a bot wall), so this rests on three rival pages, not all of them.
decides: It doesn't change the pick, but it adds a sourced cheapest option. If the shopper only wants file storage and backups with 2.5GbE, the UNAS 2 at $199 from the maker beats every 2.5GbE option ChatGPT showed. The tradeoff, which our current page already sources to NASCompares, is that it runs no Docker, no VMs and no app store. Anyone who wants Plex or Docker still lands on the F2-425 or F2-423, or the DXP2800 if its sub-$300 price is real. I could not open any store page to confirm the $296.99 DXP2800 price. Both rival pages that price it say $389.99, so the page should not treat $296.99 as a regular price.
